<title>Specialized high schools in New York City</title>
<fragment>

Their status as specialized schools was frequently threatened by factions within the New York City school system and government. As a way to preserve their special status, in 1972, the Hecht-Calandra Act was passed by the New York State Legislature, designating these schools as specialized science and math high schools for New York City. The Act called for a uniform exam in math and science to be administered for admission to these schools, in keeping with the uniform examination that had already been required by the New York City Board of Education for admission to these schools. The School of Performing Arts and The High School of Music & Art (consolidated in 1984 into LaGuardia High School) were also designated by the legislature as specialized high schools, and admission was by audition and portfolio rather than examination, in keeping with their artistic mission.[6]

Nine selective public high schools




The **specialized high schools of New York City** are nine selective public high schools, established and run by the New York City Department of Education to serve the needs of academically and artistically gifted students. The Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT) examination is required for admission to all the schools except LaGuardia, which requires an audition or portfolio for admission.[1]

All of these schools are required by state law to admit students based on the uniform Specialized High Schools Admissions Test,[7] and positions are assigned on a ranked system, depending on numbers of seats available and how many applicants requested a given school.

content:
**Specialized High Schools — NYC (Founded)**  

| School (as a Specialized High School) | Year Founded* | Notes on Founding |
|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
| **Stuyvesant High School** | **1904** | Opened as the “Manual Training School” on 23rd St. in Manhattan; renamed Stuyvesant in 1907 and later designated a Specialized High School. |
| **Bronx High School of Science** | **1938** | Began in a temporary building on East 150th St.; moved to its current campus in Bronx Park‑East in 1959. |
| **Brooklyn Technical High School** | **1922** | First classes held in the former Brooklyn Boys High School; the current “Tech” campus on Flatbush Ave. opened in 1929. |
| **Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School of Music & Art and Performing Arts** | **1984** (merger) | Formed by merging the **High School of Music & Art** (founded 1936) and the **School of Performing Arts** (founded 1948). The combined LaGuardia school is the city’s only art‑focused Specialized High School and admits students by audition/portfolio. |
| **Queens High School for the Sciences at York College (QHSSYC)** | **2002** | Opened in 2002 as the newest science‑oriented Specialized High School, sharing a campus with York College (CUNY). |
| **High School of American Studies at Lehman College (HSAS)** | **2002** | Launched in 2002 on the Lehman College (CUNY) campus; focuses on a rigorous humanities curriculum. |
| **High School for Math, Science and Engineering at City College (HSMSE)** | **2002** | Opened in 2002 on the City College (CUNY) campus; emphasizes STEM and engineering. |
| **Brooklyn Latin School** | **2006** | Established in 2006 as the city’s first public school with a classical‑liberal‑arts curriculum; admitted by SHSAT. |
| **Staten Island Technical High School** | **1982** (as annex) → **1988** (independent) | Began in 1982 as an annex of Ralph R. McKee Vocational‑Technical HS; became an independent Specialized High School in May 1988. |

\*The “year founded” refers to the date the school first opened **as a distinct institution** that later became (or was created as) a Specialized High School. For schools that resulted from a merger (e.g., LaGuardia) the merger year is listed, with the original founding dates noted in the “Notes” column.

### Quick Reference

- **Old‑est specialized schools** – Stuyvesant (1904), Bronx Science (1938), Brooklyn Tech (1922).  
- **2002 “new wave”** – QHSSYC, HSAS, HSMSE were all opened the same year to broaden the specialized‑school portfolio.  
- **Most recent additions** – Brooklyn Latin (2006) and Staten Island Tech (independent 1988, but its origins date to 1982).  

All of the above schools are administered by the **New York City Department of Education** and (except LaGuardia) admit students based on the **Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT)**.
